title: Requirements for spatialcovariates R Package
text: document outlines requirements developing new R package called spatialcovariates. package provide automated functions fetch, process, stack environmental covariates commonly used Plot2Map workflows bias modeling uncertainty quantification (e.g., demonstrated Mexico AGB mapping notebook). package focuses reproducibility : - Prioritizing STAC-compatible catalogs querying downloading data. - Clipping rasters user-specified extent (e.g., country boundary). - Resampling/aggregating target resolution (e.g., 10 km match ESA CCI AGB maps). - Handling fallbacks non-STAC sources (e.g., direct FTP downloads shapefile rasterization). implemented, package can imported Plot2Map (e.g., via library(spatialcovariates)) used functions like extractBiasCovariates() passing stacked covariates. Target Users: Plot2Map developers users analyzing AGB maps globally regionally. Package Structure: - DESCRIPTION: Standard R package metadata (Title: “Automated Covariate Fetching Plot2Map Bias Modeling”; Version: 0.1.0; Depends: R (>= 4.0); Imports: terra, sf, rstac, httr, etc.). - R/: Core functions (detailed ). - man/: Rd documentation exported functions. - tests/: Unit tests function (e.g., using testthat). - README.md: Installation, usage examples (including Mexico demo), citations. - vignettes initially; add one full workflow integration.

title: Requirements for spatialcovariates R Package
text: package must fully CRAN-compatible facilitate easy submission maintenance. Key requirements include: R CMD Check Compliance: Pass R CMD check ---cran zero errors, zero warnings, zero notes least R versions 4.0+ (test via devtools::check() rcmdcheck). Documentation Standards: Use roxygen2 Rd files; ensure @examples executable non-interactive (plotting unless wrapped (interactive())). Follow tidyverse style guide (e.g., via lintr styler). calls install.packages(), library() functions; use requireNamespace() optional deps. Avoid packageStartupMessage() .onLoad(); use utils::packageDescription() version checks sparingly. functions must handle missing arguments gracefully defaults. Testing Coverage: Aim >80% code coverage via testthat; include tests edge cases (e.g., invalid extents, offline mode). Support R >= 4.0 DESCRIPTION. Include NEWS.md changelog (even v0.1.0). License: MIT (explicitly state DESCRIPTION include LICENSE file). Platform Independence: Ensure platform-specific code (e.g., test Linux/Mac/Windows via rhub::check_for_cran()). Submission Readiness: finalizing, run devtools::spell_check() spelling, devtools::release() dry-run, validate CRAN’s repository policies (e.g., external binaries).

title: Requirements for spatialcovariates R Package
text: Implement function R/Covariates.R. functions : - Accept extent (sf polygon numeric bbox vector). - Accept year (numeric, default 2010 match notebook). - Accept resolution (character, e.g., “10km”; compute aggregation factor based native res). - Accept outdir (character, optional; save processed rasters GeoTIFF). - Return terra::rast (list paired outputs). - Include verbose logging (e.g., cat() progress). - Handle errors gracefully (e.g., STAC fails, try direct download). - Document @param, @return, @examples Rd format.

title: Requirements for spatialcovariates R Package
text: Purpose: Fetch ESA CCI Biomass AGB SD maps (v3, 2010). Source: MAAP STAC catalog (esa-cci-biomass-l4-v3). Use rstac::stac("https://stac-browser.maap-project.org"). Query stac_search(collections = "esa-cci-biomass-l4-v3", bbox = st_bbox(extent), datetime = paste0(year, "-01-01/", year, "-12-31")). Fetch assets: agb sd (NetCDF). Crop extent using terra::crop(). resolution == "10km", aggregate terra::aggregate(fact = 3, fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE) (approx. native ~3 km 10 km). Output: Named list list(agb = rast, sd = rast). Filename Save: agb_{year}_10km.tif, sd_{year}_10km.tif.

title: Requirements for spatialcovariates R Package
text: Purpose: Fetch Global Forest Canopy Height (Potapov et al., 2021; ~2010, 30m). Source: MAAP/GLAD STAC (glad-glclu2020-change-v2 gfch); fallback GLAD FTP tiles. STAC query https://stac-browser.maap-project.org collections including height asset. Crop aggregate resolution (fact ~3 30m → 10km, mean). Fallback: Download tiles covering extent GLAD FTP (implement tile-listing helper). Output: rast (height meters). Filename Save: height_10km.tif.

title: Requirements for spatialcovariates R Package
text: Purpose: Fetch rasterize RESOLVE Ecoregions biomes (Dinerstein et al., 2017; static). Source: Direct shapefile download https://ecoregions.appspot.com/ecoregions.zip. Download unzip tempdir. Read sf::st_read("ecoregions.shp"). Rasterize BIOME_NUM field initial 10km grid using terra::rasterize(vect(ecoreg["BIOME_NUM"]), rast(extent, resolution = 10000), field = "BIOME_NUM"). Mask extent. Output: rast (biome classes integers). Filename Save: Ecoregions2017_biome.tif.

title: Requirements for spatialcovariates R Package
text: Purpose: Fetch Global Tree Canopy Cover (Sexton et al., 2015; 30m, 2015). Source: UMD GLCF FTP (ftp://ftp.glcf.umd.edu/glcf/Global_TreeCover/v3/2015/); fallback GEE via rgee. Identify download tiles covering extent (implement list_tiles_for_extent() helper based lon/lat grid). Mosaic terra::mosaic(). Crop extent; aggregate resolution (mean). Output: rast (% tree cover). Filename Save: TC_Sexton_2015_10km.tif.

title: Requirements for spatialcovariates R Package
text: Purpose: Fetch SRTM V3 DEM compute slope/aspect. Source: OpenTopography STAC (otsrtm.042013.4326.1). STAC query https://portal.opentopography.org/api/v1/stac. Fetch DEM asset. Crop extent. Compute slope <- terra::terrain(dem, "slope", unit = "degrees"); aspect <- terra::terrain(dem, "aspect", unit = "degrees"). Aggregate resolution (mean). Output: Named list list(slope = rast, aspect = rast). Filename Save: slope_10km.tif, aspect_10km.tif.

title: Requirements for spatialcovariates R Package
text: Purpose: Fetch Intact Forest Landscapes (2016; binary). Source: OpenLandMap STAC (forest.cover_esacci.ifl). STAC query https://stac.openlandmap.org datetime 2016. Fetch IFL asset (binary: 1 = intact). Crop extent; aggregate resolution (sum > 0 binary). Output: rast (binary). Filename Save: ifl_16.tif.

title: Requirements for spatialcovariates R Package
text: Purpose: Orchestrate fetching covariates stack . Call functions sequentially. Stack c(...); name layers: "agb", "height", "biome", "treecover", "slope", "aspect", "ifl". Note: Use 2015/2016 tree cover/IFL despite year param (document year mismatches). Output: SpatRaster stack. Integration Note: Export main user-facing function; suggest calling Plot2Map’s data loading sections.

title: Automated Covariate Fetching for Plot2Map
text: Automated Covariate Fetching Plot2Map Bias Modeling spatialcovariates provides automated functions fetch, process, stack environmental covariates commonly used Plot2Map workflows bias modeling uncertainty quantification forest biomass mapping.

title: Automated Covariate Fetching for Plot2Map
text: Multi-source data integration: Download ESA CCI, GLAD, RESOLVE, UMD GLCF, CGIAR-CSI, Intact Forests One-line workflows: Single function fetch stack covariates Reproducible pipelines: Standardized spatial processing (crop, resample, aggregate) Parallel downloads: Speed data acquisition multi-core support Smart caching: Avoid redundant downloads local file management API keys required: data public sources CRAN-ready: Fully documented comprehensive testing

title: Automated Covariate Fetching for Plot2Map
text: Install development version GitHub:
code: # install.packages("devtools") devtools::install_github("aTnT/spatialcovariates")

title: Automated Covariate Fetching for Plot2Map
text: simplest workflow uses getBiasCovariates() download stack environmental covariates:
code: library(spatialcovariates)  # Define region of interest (Mexico example) mexico_bbox <- c(xmin = -118, ymin = 14, xmax = -86, ymax = 33)  # Fetch all covariates at 10km resolution covariates <- getBiasCovariates(   extent = mexico_bbox,   year = 2010,   resolution = "10km",   n_cores = 4  # Use 4 cores for parallel downloads )  # View the stack plot(covariates) names(covariates) # [1] "agb"       "height"    "biome"     "treecover" # [5] "slope"     "aspect"    "ifl"

title: Automated Covariate Fetching for Plot2Map
text: Use fetched covariates directly Plot2Map workflows:
code: library(Plot2Map)  # Extract bias covariates for your plot data bias_model <- extractBiasCovariates(   plot_data = my_field_plots,   map_agb_raster = covariates[["agb"]],   covariate_rasters = covariates[[c("height", "biome", "treecover",                                     "slope", "aspect", "ifl")]] )

what: ESA CCI Biomass (AGB and Standard Deviation)
title: Automated Covariate Fetching for Plot2Map
code: # Fetch AGB and SD for 2010 biomass <- getESACCIAGB(   extent = mexico_bbox,   year = 2010,   version = "v3.0",   resolution = "10km" )  # Access individual layers agb <- biomass$agb    # Aboveground biomass (Mg/ha) sd <- biomass$sd      # Standard deviation (Mg/ha)

title: Automated Covariate Fetching for Plot2Map
code: # Fetch Potapov height data height <- getPotapovHeight(   extent = mexico_bbox,   resolution = "10km" )  plot(height, main = "Forest Canopy Height (m)")

title: Automated Covariate Fetching for Plot2Map
code: # Fetch RESOLVE Ecoregions biomes biomes <- getDinersteinBiome(   extent = mexico_bbox,   resolution = "10km" )  # Biome codes: 1-14 (see ?getDinersteinBiome for details) plot(biomes, main = "RESOLVE Biomes")

title: Automated Covariate Fetching for Plot2Map
code: # Fetch Sexton tree cover for 2015 treecover <- getSextonTreeCover(   extent = mexico_bbox,   year = 2015,   resolution = "10km" )  plot(treecover, main = "Tree Cover (%)")

title: Automated Covariate Fetching for Plot2Map
code: # Fetch SRTM terrain derivatives terrain <- getSRTMTerrain(   extent = mexico_bbox,   resolution = "10km" )  par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) plot(terrain$slope, main = "Slope (degrees)") plot(terrain$aspect, main = "Aspect (degrees)")

title: Automated Covariate Fetching for Plot2Map
code: # Fetch IFL 2016 ifl <- getIFL(   extent = mexico_bbox,   year = 2016,   resolution = "10km" )  plot(ifl, main = "Intact Forest Landscapes (1 = intact)")

title: Automated Covariate Fetching for Plot2Map
text: Fetch specific covariates:
code: # Fetch only AGB, height, and terrain covariates <- getBiasCovariates(   extent = mexico_bbox,   year = 2010,   resolution = "10km",   include_biome = FALSE,   include_treecover = FALSE,   include_ifl = FALSE )

title: Automated Covariate Fetching for Plot2Map
text: Avoid re-downloading using local files:
code: # First download covariates <- getBiasCovariates(   extent = mexico_bbox,   download = TRUE,   data_dir = "my_data"  # Save tiles here )  # Later: reprocess without downloading covariates_new <- getBiasCovariates(   extent = mexico_bbox,   download = FALSE,   data_dir = "my_data"  # Use existing tiles )

title: Automated Covariate Fetching for Plot2Map
text: Save processed covariates disk:
code: covariates <- getBiasCovariates(   extent = mexico_bbox,   year = 2010,   resolution = "10km",   outdir = "output/processed"  # Saves all layers as GeoTIFFs )

title: Automated Covariate Fetching for Plot2Map
text: Use different extent formats:
code: library(sf)  # From sf polygon mexico <- st_read("countries.shp") %>%   filter(name == "Mexico") covariates <- getBiasCovariates(extent = mexico)  # From terra SpatVector mexico_vect <- vect(mexico) covariates <- getBiasCovariates(extent = mexico_vect)  # From numeric bbox bbox <- c(xmin = -118, ymin = 14, xmax = -86, ymax = 33) covariates <- getBiasCovariates(extent = bbox)
